issues.description: Conceptual entity mismatch between artifacts: the problem statement/UML defines a class named "Meal" (and SealSaloon methods/fields use Meal), but the template repository provides an "Order" class with the same structure (name + ingredients) and an empty Meal.java file. This can mislead students into using/implementing the wrong class name and breaks compilation when implementing SealSaloon against the specification (Meal vs Order).
issues.suggestedFix: Make naming consistent across all artifacts. Preferred: remove/rename template Order.java to Meal.java (class name + constructor) and update template Main.java comments accordingly. Alternatively, update the problem statement/UML and all method signatures to consistently use Order instead of Meal.

issues.description: Stock exposes an extra public API not described by the UML/spec: the problem statement lists only add/take/findStockIngredient/addToStockIngredients/emptyStock, but both template and solution include a public setStockIngredients(StockIngredient[]) method. This conflicts with the specified interface and encourages bypassing the intended stock-management workflow.
issues.suggestedFix: Either (a) update the UML/problem statement to include setStockIngredients as an allowed method (and clarify it is only for manual testing), or (b) remove it / reduce its visibility (e.g., package-private) and adjust any example code to use addToStockIngredients or SealSaloon.acceptSupplyDelivery instead.
